outcome: myelin-related proteins (MBP, MAG, MOG) gene and protein levels
cohort: The study involved 40 pregnant rats and their male and female offspring, divided into control, vitamin E, acrylamide, and acrylamide + vitamin E groups.
finding: Acrylamide administration during gestation, lactation, and post-lactation significantly disrupted myelination in offspring rats by decreasing gene and protein levels of myelin-related proteins (MBP, MAG, MOG), an effect that was improved by vitamin E.
